title: KVzip: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression with Context Reconstruction

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract states 'FlashAttention decoding latency improvements up to 1.5×', while the introduction claims 'approximately 2× latency reduction in FlashAttention' and Figure 8a shows an attention latency reduction from 0.39 ms to 0.17 ms, corresponding to a >2× speedup. This inconsistency in the reported improvement factor across sections misrepresents the actual gains.

The text first claims 'total complexity O(m n_c), linear with context length', then immediately states 'FlashAttention incurs O(n_c m + m^2/2) causal-attention FLOPs per chunk, resulting in a total complexity of O(n_c^2 + n_c m/2) across all n_c/m chunks. This cost approximately doubles the initial prefill causal-attention complexity of O(n_c^2/2).' The actual complexity is quadratic (O(n_c^2)), not linear. The contradictory statements render the complexity analysis erroneous.

Equation (2) defines S_{l,h}[j] = max_{g=1,...,G; i=1,...,n_c} \bar{A}_{l,h}[g, j, i], but \bar{A}_{l,h} has dimensions G × n_c × n_in. The maximization over the input dimension should be i=1,...,n_in, not n_c. This is a dimension mismatch and an error in the mathematical formulation.

The abstract claims 'context lengths up to 100K tokens', but the experimental section explicitly states contexts up to 170K tokens (e.g., Qwen2.5-7B-1M with Retr.KV and other tasks). The abstract significantly understates the maximum context length used in evaluations, misrepresenting the scope of the experiments.

The paper claims 'privacy risks where compressed KV caches leak sensitive information omitted by full caches', but Table 1, the only provided example, shows identical responses from full and evicted caches with no leakage. No other evidence of privacy leakage is presented. The claim is therefore completely unsupported and misleading.
